Finally! After 2 months of starting my Kaito journey, I’ve hit my first 50+ YAPS🔥

I wouldn’t have reached this without the support and motivation from my @virtuals_io fam. Most of these YAPs came from my organic interactions within the Virtuals ecosystem. I still remember the day I got the most YAPs (+13) it came from @VaderResearch. I didn’t expect that huge amount, but maybe that’s what happens when you’re not expecting anything at all.

I’ve met a lot of cool people, not just in the English community, but also in the KR and CN communities. Thank you!

Of course, some of my @overtake_world friends are still actively engaging in my timeline. August is coming, and it’s almost time for us to receive our TAKE rewards!

Right now, I’m starting to make friends and be part of new communities. I’ve already met some helpful homies in @SonicEcosystem. Sadly, I missed joining the @Bybit_Official Kaito Earn campaign. It’s ending in a week, but a friend motivated me to still give it a shot since not many are talking about it yet.

Lastly, I’m starting my @shoutdotfun journey today, I heard this one’s going to cook. Some of my friends are already earning just by SHOUT-ing and giving their best ENERGY. Better late than NEVER!

That’s my morning update for now. There’s heavy rain and flooding here in PH, if you’re from the Philippines too, STAY SAFEF FAM!

Have a great day, EVERYONE

🇺🇸 U.S. Market Summary | Tuesday, July 22, 2025

The U.S. stock market ended mixed today.

The S&P 500 hit another all-time high despite weakness in tech stocks, as funds rotated into defensive sectors such as healthcare and materials. Over 400 stocks in the S&P 500 finished higher, although the ‘Magnificent 7’ index declined for the first time in nine sessions.

However, corporate earnings showed mixed results:
•Lockheed Martin plunged 11% after reporting Q2 revenue below expectations.
•General Motors (GM) dropped 8.1% after revealing an $1.1 billion hit from tariffs, intensifying market concerns about Trump’s trade policies.

The semiconductor sector also remained under pressure.
Investor sentiment weakened following a Wall Street Journal report that SoftBank and OpenAI’s $500 billion AI initiative, Project Stargate, was facing difficulties.
After hours, Texas Instruments released disappointing guidance, adding to the sector’s headwinds.

Still, the overall earnings season remains strong.
According to FactSet, 85% of S&P 500 companies that have reported so far have beaten expectations.
Investors are now closely watching for forward guidance on macroeconomic risks, tariff impacts, and AI-related demand.

⸻

🌐 Trade Uncertainty & Geopolitics
•President Trump announced a finalized trade agreement with the Philippines, while Canada’s Prime Minister stated they are working to stabilize relations with the U.S.
•Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed a 3rd round of trade talks with China in Stockholm next week to discuss a tariff ceasefire extension.
•Bessent also stated there would be no changes in Fed Chair Powell’s position, though Trump continues to push for a 3 percentage point rate cut.

⸻

📊 Market Commentary
•Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi (UBS Global):
“The threat to Fed independence and lingering geopolitical risk could increase market volatility as we approach the August 1 tariff deadline.”
•Kevin Gordon (Charles Schwab):
“The recent modest rally suggests valuations may be stretched.”
•Ross Mayfield (Baird):
“Markets are in wait-and-see mode ahead of the August 1 tariff deadline and key earnings from the Magnificent 7.”

“Water flow regulation by forests reduces potential floodwater generation in watersheds and in areas downstream of watersheds, thereby reducing the risk of flooding.

Higher forest cover can help reduce the volume of floodwater generated in a watershed by 27% to 47% during the three wettest months of the year compared to a ‘No Forest’ cover simulation in the UMRBPL.”

[Note: The Upper Marikina River Basin Protected Landscape currently only has ~25% forest cover based on available data, despite being protected by law since 1904.]

-From Rawlins et al., 2017. Understanding the Role of Forests in Supporting Livelihoods and Climate Resilience: Case Studies in the Philippines. World Bank: Manila, Philippines.
